title: Sourcing App With Curate Document And Beams Windows Slabs Modules
description: Create a new app technology `sourcing` for handpicking and curating 3D object kinds (not instances) out of a catalogue. Each object kind has an availability count and follows a typology (tree). Sourcing has modules (beams, windows, slabs) contributed as separate plugin crates via a new Contribution::SourcingModule variant. The curate document (stock, filters, curated set) is edited through a 3-column UI: left = filtered pool table, middle = curated table (top) + 3D preview of last selection (bottom), right = 3D grid of all filtered kinds scaled to fit. Tables need +/- availability steppers and cross-window drag-and-drop, requiring extending the framework's declarative TableScene/table-host (React + wgpu parity) with typed cells, selection, sort, and drag/drop support. Register the new technology across Cargo.toml, package.json, repo/lib/js/index.ts, framework/core/js/index.ts, launch.json files, and s/manifest/resources.manifest.json.
summary:
Built the `sourcing` app end-to-end: a curate workflow for handpicking 3D object kinds (beams/windows/slabs) out of a modular catalogue, verified working live in the browser dev preview.

**Framework extensions** (root-level, reusable by every app): added `Contribution::SourcingModule` to `framework/core/rs/lib.rs` for modules to contribute a typology tree + catalogue kinds to a host app via the existing plugin-manifest contribution channel. Extended `TableScene` with `selectionJson`/`rowDragMime`/`dropAction`/`sortJson` plus a new `TableCell` enum (Text/Number/Stepper/Buttons) and `table_row_json` builder, with a `TableScene::base()` constructor migration across all existing callers (trinity, imperative, core tests) — old 2-field JSON still round-trips unchanged. Wired the new cell/selection/sort/drag vocabulary through both renderers: React's `table-host.tsx` (+ a `rowDragProps` hook added to the shared `Table` component in `ui/js/react/index.tsx` for cross-window HTML5 drag, independent of the existing dnd-kit intra-table reordering) and the wgpu renderer's `render_table`. Generalized the plugin registry scanner (`framework/plugin/registry/script.ts`) from a `forms/module`-specific special case to a general `*/module/*/rs` pattern so any technology's module crates auto-register.

**Sourcing crates**: `sourcing/curate/rs` (domain: typology trees, geometry recipes → mesh generation, filters/curated-set logic, grid layout math), three contributor plugin crates `sourcing/module/{beams,windows,slabs}/rs` (each contributing a typology + demo catalogue kinds), and the host `sourcing/plugin/rs` (3-column window layout — pool table | curated table + 3D preview | 3D grid — with filter UI, drag-and-drop wiring, and full action handling). Registered across root `Cargo.toml`, `package.json` (`dev:sourcing`), `.claude/launch.json` and `.vscode/launch.json` (ports 6081 react / 6181 wgpu), and `s/manifest/resources.manifest.json`.

**Mid-flight architecture migration**: partway through, another concurrent session landed a large breaking change to the `PluginApp` trait (moving every app from stateless `document_json: &str` handling to a typed `DocumentApp` trait wrapped in `VcsDocumentApp` with real CRDT-style operations/inverses, following `process3d`'s already-migrated reference implementation). Migrated `sourcing_curate`/`sourcing-plugin` to match: added `SourcingOp`/`SourcingDiff` (a wholesale-document-swap `Operation` impl, since every sourcing action already recomputes the full document) and rewrote the app to `impl DocumentApp`. All 5 sourcing crates compile and their unit tests pass (32 tests total) against the new architecture.

**Unrelated regressions fixed while getting the dev server running** (both blocking every app, not just sourcing, so fixed at the root rather than worked around): a stale relative path in `mathematical/graph/drawing/rs/Cargo.toml` (`../../geometry/rs` → `../../../geometry/rs`, one directory level short after a crate move); and two missing exports (`resolvePluginRegistryId`, `resolvePlaygroundDefaultAppId`) that `framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx` still imported from `framework/core/js/index.ts` after another session removed the old hardcoded lookup maps in favor of the new Cargo.toml-metadata-driven playground catalog — restored both functions sourced from the new generated `PLAYGROUND_BUILD_TARGETS` catalog instead of the old hardcoded maps, fixing every app's dev-server boot, not just sourcing's.

**Verified live**: `bun run dev:sourcing` boots cleanly on port 6081; drove the actual UI in-browser — 3-column layout renders, module/typology/search filters work, pool and curated tables render with working +/− steppers and remove buttons, row selection syncs live across the pool table, curated table, 3D preview, and 3D grid, the 3D grid renders real per-kind geometry (beams/window-frames/slabs) correctly laid out and scaled, and the search filter reactively narrows both the table and the grid. Zero console errors throughout the session.

**Known follow-up**: the drag-and-drop UX (pool↔curated) is wired (drag source `_drag`/`rowDragMime` on rows, `dropAction`/`onDragOver`/`onDrop` on the table host) but wasn't drag-tested live in this session — click-based interactions (select, stepper, remove, filter) were all verified instead. The wgpu renderer's table parity (cells/steppers/drag-source) was unit/compile verified but not browser-driven (only the react renderer was booted).
